mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which raises wage pressures and input costs, ultimately compressing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained deceleration in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 shows two consecutive quarterly declines
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of two consecutive quarterly GDP declines.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual monetary tightening and inflationary pressure, which increases uncertainty and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the average return is not significantly negative at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A co-movement between payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) where PAYEMS rises while UNRATE falls by more than 0.3 percentage points in the same month signals a robust labor market recovery, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases by >0.3pp in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in more than 60% of triggered months, or the median return is not statistically greater than zero.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and consumer confidence, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of four consecutive months with HOUST above its 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals reduced household savings and increased consumption financed by debt, which temporarily supports corporate revenues but ultimately raises default risk and uncertainty, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 12-month moving average for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of three consecutive months with RSAFS below its 12-month moving average.
